reasoning.text: The render now passes both acceptance tests. ISO shows the open, fully populated eight-lane butterfly array with no opaque block swallowing a subsystem; TOP confirms all eight blue BRAM banks, the copper DSP multiplier column as a clean vertical row of dots, the two distinct reduction members (cylindrical Barrett spine + boxy shift/subtract), the brass twiddle rail/feeder L, both white FIFOs, and the right-edge ROM/addr-gen/controller cluster; FRONT/SIDE show the exploded heatsink fan and the exploded butterfly lane riding correctly on its two grounded risers. The only residual nit is that the lifted exploded cluster previously hovered over the dead-center lanes in plan view; I shifted it toward the +Z half so the central lanes read in TOP. All carried-over gaps (8-of-8 butterfly units, a cylindrical Barrett silhouette, and an explicit operand-return path) are already closed by the current read/return buses with direction arrows.

fields.before: EXPLODED VIEW floating above the array on two riser posts, offset in Z so it clears the central lanes in plan view: one of the eight identical butterfly lanes lifted off the board to expose its left-to-right datapath (DSP multiply -> symmetric add/sub -> pipeline register).
fields.after: EXPLODED VIEW floating above the array on two riser posts, offset toward the +Z half of the array so it clears the central lanes (3-4) in plan view: one of the eight identical butterfly lanes lifted off the board to expose its left-to-right datapath (DSP multiply -> symmetric add/sub -> pipeline register).

meta.before: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic. 2) Along the left edge mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks at 1.1 m pitch and flank them with the forward-NTT input FIFO and the natural-order output FIFO. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Lay one shared open butterfly-array baseplate across the array, then populate it with eight parallel butterfly clusters (one per BRAM bank); inside each cluster wire the DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder (dark anodized) and subtractor (brushed steel), then both into the pipeline register. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar, and route the operand-read bus from the crossbar east into the multiplier column; cap each with a direction arrow so the read/twiddle/return dataflow triad is fully visible and the conflict-free read-modify-write loop is closed. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM and route a brass broadcast feeder west to the rail spanning the multiplier column so one fetched factor fans out to all eight multipliers; then add the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one butterfly cluster onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array (multiply->add/sub->register), offset in Z so it clears the central lanes in plan view, and clamp the seven-fin exploded aluminum heatsink onto its riser stub above the die.
